## Sonic Fangames Find New Life

The indie fan game community is buzzing with two distinct titles launching recently. On the more polished end, *Chao Racing Trials*, developed by KetrinDarkDragon, has captured attention on Bluesky, Newsblur, and Tumblr. Hosted on the Sonic Fangames HQ forums, the game offers a straightforward racing loop where players collect Chao characters and hats. Multiple prominent accounts, including @sonichedgeblog, have amplified the release, signaling strong community enthusiasm for this new entry in the Sonic modding space.

In stark contrast, user kbmodo has introduced *FartPuzzler*, another Sonic-inspired title that leans heavily into comedy and visceral mechanics. Showcased on the same forums, the game challenges players to manage farting, pooping, rotating, and mashing actions within a puzzle framework. While smaller in scope than *Chao Racing Trials*, the quirky nature of *FartPuzzler* has found a dedicated niche audience eager for something offbeat and humorous.

## Decentralized Social Media: PDS Visibility

A technical discussion on Bluesky has emerged regarding how Personal Data Servers (PDSs) are presented to users. Bailey Townsend is currently refining the visibility of PDSs, choosing to hide those with "bad actors" while ensuring they remain accessible via their direct URLs for easy migration. The goal is to balance user safety with discoverability. Evan Jarrett has jumped in to suggest utilizing the "well-known" tag to optionally hide specific servers, highlighting the ongoing challenge for developers to create intuitive interfaces for the decentralized social ecosystem without sacrificing transparency.

## AI Regulation and the "Cult-Like" Narrative

Debate continues over the direction of Artificial Intelligence policy. User @Doll argues that public outrage over recent AI outputs, referred to here as "glozo" (likely a typo for "glow-up"), is being exploited by powerful entities to justify deep restrictions on the technology. The core of the argument is that regulators aim to ban open-source AI, effectively confining the tech to a "cult-like" ingroup of large corporations. @Doll points to data center expansions as visual proof of this agenda and urges followers to resist becoming pawns in the push toward AI elitism.

Meanwhile, tension simmers in gaming communities. The chaotic launch of a new Paper Mario port has led to a influx of speculation on the official Discord. Moderators are actively deleting comments questioning whether assets were LLM-generated. Observers on Bluesky find the irony hilarious, noting how a traditional Nintendo release is facing the same AI skepticism as indie titles, underscoring the growing friction between players and publishers regarding technology integration.

## Political Economy: Trump on Tariffs

Former President Donald Trump reinforced his stance on international trade, asserting that the US does not lose $50 billion annually in trade with tariff-imposing countries. His logic is simple: cutting off trade entirely eliminates that loss. This claim serves as a pillar for his broader argument for imposing high tariffs across all imports, positioning them as a protection for domestic industries rather than a burden on consumers. The statement highlights his continued focus on bilateral trade deficits as a key metric of economic success.

## Community Whispers

*   **Will Ferrell Lookalike:** User @emily s. shared a momentary confusion on Bluesky, noting that a stranger wearing a hat bore a striking resemblance to Will Ferrell. The post captures a fleeting celebrity illusion triggered by a specific hairstyle.
*   **Myanmar’s Scheme:** @Evergreen Intel expressed strong disapproval of an unnamed "awful" scheme, suspecting Myanmar as the culprit. The post suggests a distinctive strategy in governance or infrastructure, sparking niche debate over its origin.
*   **Faw’s Lonely Heart:** In r/FAW, a 20-year-old disabled woman vented about a romantic triangle. She convinced herself a new male friend was interested, only to find he had liked another friend for a year. Complicating matters, a third friend confessed a crush on the same guy. Feeling isolated and hoping her self-esteem wasn’t tied to her rejection, she debated revealing her theory but decided against it to avoid looking "mean."
*   **4chan’s Wall Strategy:** On /p/, a user recommended dominating the board by taking rapid 40fps snapshots of a featureless wall at Metropolitan Federal Court. The strategy relies on boredom and efficiency, generating a year’s worth of content from a single nondescript location.
*   **Ban Drama:** Another /p/ user received a permanent ban after posting a cartoon in the Recent Photos thread. The community is debating the severity of the punishment for what they perceive as a simple submission, highlighting ongoing tension with moderators.
*   **Fgt Deflection:** On /fgt/, a user tired of an internet spat instructed others to read replies carefully before engaging, calling those continuing the debate "foolish." The post reflects a sense of weariness with redundant conflict.

representative_texts: @WolfieGirlXox - FAW, a women-only sub — 20, Disabled, Never Had Anything Close to a Romantic interaction and The Guy I Thought Might Like Me Likes My Friend — Hey guys, this is mostly a vent I guess but I would love any support/advice/encouragement/whatever y'all can give. I might delete this later tbh.   So here goes. I (20F) have never had anything even close to a romantic interaction. I've never been confessed to, hit on, flirted with, kissed, dated, none of that. I've never even been cat called or anything. I am visibly disabled/deformed. I will not go into detail on this but it impacts the way my face looks in such a way that people can tell at a glance I'm not "normal."   For the last year or so ish I've been really feeling the lack of romance in my life, I've always had phases of wanting a partner really bad, listening to love songs, looking at dating advice, etc. but I feel like it's been happening way more lately to the point it's genuinely affecting my mental health. I spend so much time longing for love, even to just have someone I don't even like express even a crumb of interest in me would make me feel so much better, but as time goes on it feels more and more like that may never be a possibility for me.   That brings me to now, to the very emotionally complicated situation I've found myself in. As a weird sort of byproduct of the yearning for romance my brain has started looking for any signs that any guy around me might like me even a little bit. Well, this week my "most likely case" and really the only one with any merit was disproven.   This guy is a friend of a friend who has been slowly working into our friend group since he transferred to our school this year. I know from things my friend has told us that he is single, interested in girls, and actively looking for a relationship. So, when he started hanging around smaller groups I was in I took note and started paying attention. I had myself convinced that this guy might like me, I was far from certain, and definitely not the best person to ask about these sorts of things, but he listened when I spoke and asked attentive follow-up questions, something that, to my understanding, is not something straight men do with women they aren't interested in.   Today, one of my other friends told me that she has a crush on this guy, and immediately I started thinking "oh no!" But it gets worse, because then she told me that she spoke to the friend who knows the guy I thought liked me and he told her that this guy has a crush on one of our other friends. The conversation mostly moved on to very painfully trying to comfort my friend about her crush liking some else.   I'm trying to process this, but it's difficult. I don't think I was ever even truly interested in him but still, I really let myself believe he liked me, I suppose that was silly. I'm not really sure what to do, if there even is anything to do.   I'm debating if I want to tell the friend who has a crush on him my side or not, but I feel mean trying to get comfort from her about a situation that hurts her just as much, if not more. I don't have any people irl who I can talk to about this since basically everyone is involved somewhat in this situation.   TLDR: I'm a visibly disabled 20 year old who has never had any romantic experience in my life and I managed to convince myself a guy I know likes me only to find out that not only does my friend have a crush on him, but his real crush this whole time has been one of my other friends.   Posted by u/WolfieGirlXox · [comments]
clusters.summary: @WolfieGirlXox, a 20-year-old visibly disabled woman with no prior romantic experience, posted a vent in r/FAW expressing frustration over her recent mental health decline due to romantic longing. She detailed how she convinced herself that a new male friend was interested in her after he showed attentive listening skills, only to discover he has liked another friend for a year. Complicating matters, another friend recently confessed her own crush on this same guy, creating a triangle where the protagonist feels she is "the only one" unaware of the connection. The poster debated whether to share her theory with the friend who has the crush but decided against it to avoid being perceived as mean. She described the situation as emotionally complicated, noting that while she never truly liked the guy, proving he liked someone else hurt her self-esteem. The post highlights her isolation, as she lacks other real-life friends to discuss the situation with, leaving her feeling increasingly hopeless about finding a partner.
